name: Glimepiride
summary: A second-generation sulfonylurea that stimulates pancreatic insulin secretion; a mainstay oral agent for type 2 diabetes.
mechanism: Binds the sulfonylurea receptor (SUR1) subunit of ATP-sensitive potassium channels on pancreatic beta cells, closing the channel and triggering calcium-dependent insulin secretion.
targets: SUR1/Kir6.2 ATP-sensitive potassium channel (pancreatic beta cells)
pharmacodynamics: Enhances both basal and meal-stimulated insulin secretion; efficacy requires functioning beta cells.

dosing.adult: 1–2 mg once daily with the first main meal; titrate by 1–2 mg every 1–2 weeks

safety.pregnancy: Not preferred; insulin is standard during pregnancy
warnings: Hypoglycemia, especially in elderly patients, renal impairment, or with missed meals
safety.overdose: Hypoglycemia; treat with oral or IV glucose and close monitoring

indications: Type 2 diabetes mellitus as adjunct to diet and exercise
Combination with metformin or other agents when monotherapy is insufficient
clinicalPearls: Take with the first main meal so peak drug effect aligns with the postprandial glucose peak.
CYP2C9 inhibitors (e.g., fluconazole) and inducers (e.g., rifampicin) alter hypoglycemia risk.
good: Low-cost, effective once-daily add-on when metformin alone is not enough.
bad: Renal impairment, frail elderly, or patients with high hypoglycemia risk.
